phases.name: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
phases.description: Keep the live brief intact, accept changes through explicit integrations, and return risk decisions within the stated latency target.

phases.name: Build the evidence and model foundation
phases.description: Preserve versioned change, incident, dependency, and outcome evidence for online features and offline training.

phases.name: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
phases.description: Separate risk prediction from policy enforcement; combine model evidence with collisions, blast radius, and deployment-window signals.

phases.name: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
phases.description: Measure latency, prediction quality, throughput, and incident outcomes; treat each stated target as unproven until tested.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Separate the brief from assumptions
steps.content: The frozen problem asks for historical change–incident correlation, proposed-change risk scores, detection of risky combinations, deployment-window recommendations, blast-radius prediction, outcome tracking, policy enforcement, and CI/CD plus change-management integrations. Its targets are scoring latency under 30 seconds, prediction accuracy above 85%, at least 1,000 changes per day, 40% fewer change-related incidents, and automated approval for low-risk changes. These are acceptance targets, not achieved service levels. The brief does not define traffic bursts, the accuracy metric, risk thresholds, retention, or availability; identify those as interview assumptions before sizing. No extra scale target is invented here.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Capture deployment metadata at the source
steps.content: Accept deployment, configuration, and infrastructure-change metadata from CI/CD. Require a stable change ID, service/resource scope, proposed time, artifact or diff reference, owner, and source version so retries and later outcomes can be joined safely.

component.label: CI/CD Change Sources
component.description: Existing CI/CD pipelines send versioned deployment, configuration, and infrastructure-change metadata with a stable change ID, artifact/diff reference, service scope, owner, and proposed time.

properties.purpose: Existing CI/CD pipelines send versioned deployment, configuration, and infrastructure-change metadata with a stable change ID, artifact/diff reference, service scope, owner, and proposed time.

component.highlightReason: Use the catalog CI/CD component for an existing producer; stable IDs and versioned metadata make risk decisions traceable and duplicate submissions idempotent.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Include change-management records
steps.content: Connect the change-management/release workflow as a separate producer. Preserve approval state, maintenance-window constraints, and the source record ID; reconcile it with CI/CD by the shared change ID rather than treating either system as the whole truth.

component.label: Change Management Sources
component.description: Release/change-management records provide approval state, owners, maintenance windows, and the source record ID; the integration reconciles these records with CI/CD by stable change ID.

properties.purpose: Release/change-management records provide approval state, owners, maintenance windows, and the source record ID; the integration reconciles these records with CI/CD by stable change ID.

component.highlightReason: This reuses the release-management catalog entry and covers the change-management half of the integration requirement without inventing a custom node.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Validate and authenticate incoming requests
steps.content: Put an authenticated, schema-validating API boundary in front of the service. Apply per-tenant quotas and idempotency keys, reject malformed or stale change revisions, and measure the end-to-end scoring clock against the under-30-second target.

component.label: Change Risk API Gateway
component.description: Authenticated API boundary for CI/CD and release-management clients; validates payload shape, enforces tenant quotas/idempotency, and records request latency and correlation IDs.

properties.purpose: Authenticated API boundary for CI/CD and release-management clients; validates payload shape, enforces tenant quotas/idempotency, and records request latency and correlation IDs.

component.highlightReason: Keep integration contracts and latency measurement at the edge; the 30-second limit is a target to validate, not a guarantee from this diagram.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Normalize changes before analysis
steps.content: Normalize provider-specific payloads into a versioned change envelope. Resolve service ownership, artifact/diff references, proposed timing, and schema version; persist an idempotency key so duplicate webhook deliveries cannot create conflicting assessments.

component.label: Change Intake and Orchestration
component.description: Normalizes CI/CD and change-management payloads into a versioned, idempotent change envelope and coordinates synchronous risk evaluation plus asynchronous evidence/outcome events.

properties.purpose: Normalizes CI/CD and change-management payloads into a versioned, idempotent change envelope and coordinates synchronous risk evaluation plus asynchronous evidence/outcome events.

component.highlightReason: A single bounded orchestration boundary supports provider adapters without coupling the model to vendor-specific webhook schemas.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Route pipeline changes through the common contract
steps.content: The gateway receives deployment and infrastructure-change submissions through one versioned contract; provider-specific parsing stays in adapters, not in risk rules.

connection.label: Versioned CI/CD change request
connection.description: Authenticated webhook/API with change ID, service scope, artifact/diff reference, proposed time, and idempotency key.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Route governed releases through the same contract
steps.content: The release/change-management integration supplies approval and calendar context without bypassing the same authentication, validation, and idempotency boundary.

connection.label: Change record and approval context
connection.description: Versioned API payload reconciled by stable change ID; preserves existing approval state and allowed maintenance windows.

steps.phase: Freeze the contract and onboard change sources
steps.title: Send normalized requests to the orchestrator
steps.content: The gateway forwards validated requests and correlation metadata. Keep model training and historical aggregation off this synchronous path so the scoring latency target is measurable and bounded.

connection.label: Validated change envelope
connection.description: Authenticated request with stable change ID, source revision, tenant, service/resource scope, timing, and correlation ID.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Buffer change and incident events durably
steps.content: Publish accepted change revisions, incident observations, policy outcomes, and final change outcomes to a durable event stream. Partition by service or another measured key so related changes can be correlated while consumers scale independently.

component.label: Change and Incident Event Bus
component.description: Durable, replayable event stream for versioned change submissions, incident observations, policy decisions, and verified outcomes; partitioning and retention are load-test assumptions.

properties.purpose: Durable, replayable event stream for versioned change submissions, incident observations, policy decisions, and verified outcomes; partitioning and retention are load-test assumptions.

component.highlightReason: Buffering absorbs bursts beyond the 1,000-per-day floor and separates online scoring from durable historical correlation; validate actual burst capacity.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Keep the versioned change and incident history
steps.content: Store immutable change revisions and join them to incident timelines, service/resource scope, deployment outcomes, and source records. Preserve event time separately from ingestion time; correct late-arriving labels without silently rewriting prior assessments.

component.label: Change and Incident History
component.description: Versioned records linking proposed and completed changes to incident timelines, active/pending service-resource scopes, source revision, prediction, policy result, and verified outcome; conditional reservations prevent concurrent proposals from both passing a stale collision check, and late labels remain auditable.

properties.purpose: Versioned records linking proposed and completed changes to incident timelines, active/pending service-resource scopes, source revision, prediction, policy result, and verified outcome; conditional reservations prevent concurrent proposals from both passing a stale collision check, and late labels remain auditable.

component.highlightReason: Historical correlation depends on reliable temporal joins and outcome provenance; a correlation is evidence for risk, not proof of causation.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Represent service and resource dependencies
steps.content: Maintain versioned service-to-service and service-to-resource edges, ownership, criticality, and environment. Compute a bounded dependency traversal for each change and expose the graph version used in every blast-radius result.

component.label: Service Dependency Graph
component.description: Versioned service/resource dependency relationships, ownership, and criticality used to estimate direct and transitive blast radius for a proposed change.

properties.purpose: Versioned service/resource dependency relationships, ownership, and criticality used to estimate direct and transitive blast radius for a proposed change.

component.highlightReason: The catalog database represents the dependency graph; no dedicated graph-provider node is required for this conceptual design.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Serve point-in-time online features
steps.content: Materialize only features available at assessment time: diff/change type, service ownership and dependencies, recent incident/change rates, timing, and current overlapping changes. Enforce point-in-time correctness to prevent future outcomes leaking into training or live inference.

component.label: Point-in-Time Change Features
component.description: Online feature service for versioned code/config change attributes, service dependencies, historical rates, timing context, and currently overlapping changes; point-in-time joins prevent label leakage.

properties.purpose: Online feature service for versioned code/config change attributes, service dependencies, historical rates, timing context, and currently overlapping changes; point-in-time joins prevent label leakage.

component.highlightReason: Feature retrieval is a bounded dependency on the synchronous path; missing or stale critical features must lower confidence or route to review rather than imply low risk.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Train from time-correct, reviewed outcomes
steps.content: Build reproducible training data from historical changes joined to incident outcomes, with temporal train/validation/test splits and review of label quality. Compare against a simple baseline, inspect class imbalance, calibrate probabilities, and reject leakage before model promotion.

component.label: Risk Model Training Pipeline
component.description: Reproducible offline training on time-correct change/incident joins and reviewed outcomes, with temporal holdouts, leakage checks, class-imbalance evaluation, calibration, and baseline comparison.

properties.purpose: Reproducible offline training on time-correct change/incident joins and reviewed outcomes, with temporal holdouts, leakage checks, class-imbalance evaluation, calibration, and baseline comparison.

component.highlightReason: The stated >85% accuracy target is not meaningful until its label, cohort, threshold, and evaluation window are defined; verify it on a temporal holdout before promotion.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Version and serve the risk model
steps.content: Serve a versioned model that estimates change risk with calibrated confidence and feature provenance. Keep model output advisory: a prediction alone never grants approval, and unknown/out-of-distribution inputs must not be labeled low-risk.

component.label: Change Risk Model
component.description: Versioned and calibrated classifier returning risk probability, confidence, model version, and feature provenance; drift or unsupported inputs are exposed for safe policy handling.

properties.purpose: Versioned and calibrated classifier returning risk probability, confidence, model version, and feature provenance; drift or unsupported inputs are exposed for safe policy handling.

component.highlightReason: A model score is evidence for the risk analysis service, not an authorization decision.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Measure outcomes by cohort and change type
steps.content: Track change volume, risk bands, approvals, incidents, rollbacks, and success by change type, team, service, and model/policy version. Compare incident rates with a defined pre-change baseline or controlled rollout; do not claim the 40% reduction from correlation alone.

component.label: Change Outcome Analytics
component.description: Cohort-based analytics for change success, incident association, risk bands, approvals, rollbacks, and model/policy versions by change type and team; supports a baseline or controlled incident-reduction evaluation.

properties.purpose: Cohort-based analytics for change success, incident association, risk bands, approvals, rollbacks, and model/policy versions by change type and team; supports a baseline or controlled incident-reduction evaluation.

component.highlightReason: This directly supports success-rate reporting while preventing an unmeasured 40% incident reduction from being presented as an outcome.

steps.phase: Build the evidence and model foundation
steps.title: Observe the full scoring path
steps.content: Measure end-to-end and dependency latency, queue lag, feature freshness, model version/drift, decision distribution, overrides, and incident outcomes. Alert on timeout or stale evidence; instrument the under-30-second and >85% targets as separate service and model-quality gates.

component.label: Risk Service Monitoring
component.description: Operational telemetry for scoring latency, queue lag, feature freshness, model drift, risk/approval distributions, overrides, and incident outcomes with alerts tied to explicit service and quality gates.

properties.purpose: Operational telemetry for scoring latency, queue lag, feature freshness, model drift, risk/approval distributions, overrides, and incident outcomes with alerts tied to explicit service and quality gates.

component.highlightReason: A latency dashboard cannot prove model accuracy, and an offline accuracy metric cannot prove the scoring SLA; keep their evidence and gates separate.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Keep risk analysis separate from authorization
steps.content: The analysis service assembles model probability, confidence, change collisions, dependency blast radius, and feasible deployment windows. It returns evidence and recommendations; a distinct policy engine decides whether the change is auto-approved, held for review, or rejected.

component.label: Risk, Collision, and Window Analysis
component.description: Combines calibrated model evidence with active-change collision detection, dependency-based blast-radius estimates, historical timing signals, and candidate deployment windows; returns a traceable recommendation, not an approval.

properties.purpose: Combines calibrated model evidence with active-change collision detection, dependency-based blast-radius estimates, historical timing signals, and candidate deployment windows; returns a traceable recommendation, not an approval.

component.highlightReason: One bounded service owns risk evidence and recommendations; keeping authorization elsewhere prevents an ML score from silently approving a production change.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Enforce versioned risk policy
steps.content: Apply explicit, versioned policy to risk band, model confidence, feature freshness, blast radius, change collisions, source approval, and permitted windows. Auto-approve only when all configured low-risk conditions hold; otherwise require a reviewer or reject. Fail closed on missing critical evidence.

component.label: Change Policy and Approval Engine
component.description: Versioned policy evaluates risk band, confidence, evidence freshness, blast radius, collisions, source approval, and permitted windows; only fully qualified low-risk changes may auto-approve, while uncertain/high-risk changes route to human review or rejection.

properties.purpose: Versioned policy evaluates risk band, confidence, evidence freshness, blast radius, collisions, source approval, and permitted windows; only fully qualified low-risk changes may auto-approve, while uncertain/high-risk changes route to human review or rejection.

component.highlightReason: This satisfies policy enforcement and low-risk automation without treating a prediction threshold as sufficient authorization.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Set safe behavior for ambiguity
steps.content: A high-risk combination means changes whose service/resource scopes overlap or whose dependency paths share a critical failure domain during overlapping execution windows. Detect the conflict before approval and recommend serialization or a safer window. Use an atomic conditional reservation keyed by the affected scope/window so two simultaneous assessments cannot both observe an empty schedule and pass. A timeout, stale graph, missing feature, low confidence, or conflicting change must never be converted to a low-risk approval; return a review-required result within the API contract.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Publish the normalized change event
steps.content: After validation, publish the versioned request and idempotency key for history, collision state, and later outcome joins. Keep the synchronous assessment response independent of downstream analytics availability.

connection.label: Versioned change event
connection.description: Partitionable event keyed by stable change/service IDs; replay supports audit and asynchronous correlation.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Persist change and incident evidence
steps.content: Consumers persist accepted revisions, incident events, model/policy outputs, and final outcomes with event-time and source provenance. Use idempotent upserts or append-only revisions for duplicate delivery and late corrections.

connection.label: Durable evidence and outcomes
connection.description: Idempotently stores change revisions, incidents, policy decisions, and verified outcomes with event-time/source metadata.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Feed incident observations into the history stream
steps.content: Incident and service-health observations become timestamped events that can be joined to changes. Correlation windows and attribution rules must be explicit; temporal association alone does not establish that a change caused an incident.

connection.label: Incident and service-health events
connection.description: Timestamped incident/SLO observations carry service scope and source IDs for later change correlation.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Build training data from verified outcomes
steps.content: The offline pipeline joins change and incident history using the label window and event-time rules, then excludes records unavailable at the original assessment time. Retain the exact dataset and model lineage for every release.

connection.label: Time-correct change/incident examples
connection.description: Offline temporal joins with reviewed labels, point-in-time feature rules, and reproducible dataset lineage.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Include measured team and change outcomes
steps.content: Use verified outcomes and human overrides as reviewed labels, not unexamined proxy targets. Preserve team/change-type cohorts so aggregate model quality cannot conceal poor performance in a risk-critical segment.

connection.label: Reviewed outcome labels
connection.description: Outcome cohorts and reviewed overrides feed offline evaluation/training with their provenance and observation windows.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Promote only a validated model version
steps.content: A candidate model reaches serving only after temporal holdout evaluation, calibration, subgroup checks, and the agreed >85% metric gate pass. Canary the new version and retain rollback to the prior version; the target is not asserted as already met.

connection.label: Validated model artifact and metrics
connection.description: Versioned artifact, feature schema, dataset lineage, calibration, and evaluation report; promotion is gated and reversible.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Materialize historical online features
steps.content: Prepare point-in-time features from the event history, including historical incident/change rates and time-window patterns. Bound feature age and expose missingness so the policy can require review when evidence is insufficient.

connection.label: Versioned historical feature values
connection.description: Point-in-time materialization of only evidence available before each assessment timestamp.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Update features from proposed changes
steps.content: Extract normalized diff/change attributes and timing context from each proposal for online feature lookup. Keep update semantics idempotent and prevent unreviewed post-change outcomes from entering the pre-change feature vector.

connection.label: Proposed-change feature request
connection.description: Versioned diff/config metadata and assessment timestamp; online features are computed without future-label leakage.

steps.phase: Score proposed changes and apply independent policy
steps.title: Combine current and historical features
steps.content: Risk analysis requests a bounded feature vector keyed by change, service, and assessment time. Enforce a timeout and freshness threshold as part of the API latency budget; missing or stale risk-critical features lead to review, not a low score.

connection.label: Bounded point-in-time feature vector
connection.description: Online change, service, history, and timing features with freshness and missingness metadata.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Estimate blast radius from the dependency graph
steps.content: The risk service receives the graph version and bounded affected-service traversal. Include owner, criticality, and shared failure-domain evidence; if topology is stale or traversal exceeds its budget, return an uncertainty/review signal.

connection.label: Versioned dependency and blast-radius evidence
connection.description: Bounded traversal result includes graph version, affected resources/services, owners, and criticality.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Resolve graph context for each change
steps.content: Resolve changed resources and service ownership against the current graph revision. Record the graph revision used so a later topology update cannot make the original blast-radius decision irreproducible.

connection.label: Resolve changed services and dependencies
connection.description: Point lookup by resource/service IDs returns ownership, graph revision, criticality, and dependency edges.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Attach model score and provenance
steps.content: The analysis service consumes the versioned model output and retains confidence, calibration, model version, and unsupported-input/drift flags with the final recommendation.

connection.label: Calibrated risk evidence
connection.description: Risk probability, confidence, model version, calibration metadata, and out-of-distribution signal.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Analyze conflicts and candidate windows
steps.content: Send each normalized change for synchronous risk analysis. Compare active/pending changes by overlapping service/resource scopes and dependency paths; use historical outcomes and calendars to rank safe windows, while preserving the under-30-second response target.

connection.label: Bounded change risk evaluation
connection.description: Synchronous request includes change scope, diff features, proposed time, active change IDs, and correlation key.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Check active change combinations
steps.content: Read active/pending change scopes and recent outcome context before declaring a proposal safe. Define collision windows and conflict precedence explicitly; serialize overlapping high-blast-radius work or return a safer candidate window.

connection.label: Active changes and historical timing context
connection.description: Bounded lookup for overlapping pending changes, prior incidents, observed outcomes, and relevant time windows; conditionally reserve the affected scope/window atomically to prevent concurrent assessments from both passing a stale read.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Pass evidence to the policy gate
steps.content: Policy consumes a complete risk package: score, confidence, graph-derived blast radius, collision status, suggested window, source approval, and evidence freshness. It evaluates explicit policy version and records its reason codes.

connection.label: Risk evidence and recommendations
connection.description: Versioned score/confidence, affected-service scope, conflict/window recommendations, source status, and evidence freshness.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Return the policy disposition to the caller
steps.content: Return a traceable disposition and reason codes through the intake/API response: auto-approved only under the low-risk policy, review-required, or rejected. Include risk score, model/policy versions, blast radius, conflicts, and recommended windows for downstream tooling.

connection.label: Decision, reason codes, and window recommendation
connection.description: Policy result returns through the same request path with score/provenance, approval state, conflict and blast-radius evidence.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Track final change outcomes
steps.content: Consume deployment completion, rollback, and later incident outcomes to calculate change success by type and team. Use a defined attribution window and preserve unresolved/censored outcomes rather than counting them as successes.

connection.label: Completion, incident, and rollback outcomes
connection.description: Asynchronous, idempotent outcome events with change ID, service/team, event time, and source provenance.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Record approval and policy outcomes
steps.content: Record auto-approvals, human decisions, policy denials, overrides, and actual deployment outcomes with the exact score and rule versions. This makes the low-risk automation and its incident impact auditable.

connection.label: Policy and approval outcome events
connection.description: Auditable disposition, rule/model versions, reviewer overrides, and subsequent verified outcome linkage.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Measure gateway latency and integration health
steps.content: Observe authentication failures, validation errors, request volume, and end-to-end latency at the entry point. Use load tests above the daily average to verify burst headroom for the 1,000+ changes/day requirement.

connection.label: Ingress latency and source health
connection.description: Request rate, p95/p99 end-to-end latency, validation failures, duplicate submissions, and per-integration health.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Monitor risk quality and safe automation
steps.content: Monitor score latency, model drift, confidence and stale-feature rates, collision detection, policy decisions, overrides, and incident outcomes. Set a pause/rollback control for model or policy releases when quality degrades; prove the 40% incident reduction with a measured baseline or controlled rollout.

connection.label: Risk quality, latency, and safety signals
connection.description: Model/policy versions, latency, feature freshness, collision decisions, overrides, drift, and outcome-quality indicators.

steps.phase: Close feedback loops and measure the targets
steps.title: Review against the frozen acceptance targets
steps.content: Before calling this design successful, define and test: end-to-end risk-scoring latency under 30 seconds at the agreed percentile and burst load; the exact >85% prediction metric on a temporal holdout and critical subgroups; capacity above 1,000 changes/day; and a causal or controlled measurement for the 40% incident-reduction target. Demonstrate that only policy-qualified low-risk changes auto-approve, while uncertain, stale, conflicting, or high-blast-radius changes require review or rejection. The walkthrough itself does not establish any target as met.
